newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHAIRMEN TO DISCUSS EVERTON JOB FOR KENDALL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHAIRMEN TO DISCUSS EVERTON JOB FOR KENDALL.

text.p: Sheffield United said on Tuesday that talks would take place between their chairman and Everton's chairman over United manager Howard Kendall's possible return to Goodison Park.
"United chairman Mike McDonald was today contacted by Everton chairman Peter Johnson and talks between the two are expected to take place today," United chief executive Charles Green said.
"When Andy Gray turned down the manager's job it was inevitable that Everton would again turn to Howard Kendall."

"It would seem that the only real matter for discussion now is the level of compensation that Everton pay for the release of Sheffield United's manager and the staff Howard Kendall would take with him to Goodison Park."
Everton remained tight-lipped on the issue. "We're making no comment in relation to the comments made by Sheffield United," a club spokesman said.

Earlier, Everton stressed they were still searching for a new manager. "If we'd appointed someone, we wouldn't be searching. I don't know of any appointment or imminent appointment," the spokesman said.
TV soccer pundit and former player Gray declined the job on Monday.

"Following the decision of Andy Gray to turn down the opportunity to manage Everton Football Club, the board met and as a result of that meeting, the search for a new manager will continue in earnest," the spokesman said.
"The next you will hear from Everton will be the appointment of a new manager."
